title: Rearranged Cipher

story.briefing: The forest gates accept a passphrase scrambled into any order, provided every character is used exactly as often as the original.
story.success: Cipher accepted. The gate reads the passphrase in whatever order you send it.

description: Given two strings, return true if one is a rearrangement of the other — that is, both contain exactly the same characters with exactly the same counts. Order does not matter. Two empty strings are rearrangements of each other. Comparison is case sensitive.
hints: Order is irrelevant, so what actually has to match is how many times each character occurs in each string.
A quick length check rules out most pairs before you count anything. And counting up for one string while counting down for the other lets you use a single map.
Return false immediately if the lengths differ. Then count each character of the first string in a map, decrement for each character of the second, and return true only if every count ends at zero.
